arxiv-2111-08155.creator: H. da Silva Jr, B. K. Kendrick, N. Balakrishnan
arxiv-2111-08155.description: Abstract Quantum calculations are reported for the stereodynamic control of the H + D 2 ⟷ {}_{2}\longleftrightarrow D + HD chemical reaction in the energy range of 1–50 K. Stereodynamic control is achieved by a formalism similar to that reported by Perreault et al. [Nature Chem.

arxiv-2201-02085.title: Exponential size scaling of the Liouvillian gap in boundary-dissipated systems with Anderson localization
arxiv-2201-02085.creator: Bozhen Zhou, Xueliang Wang, Shu Chen
arxiv-2201-02085.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Bozhen Zhou, Xueliang Wang, Shu Chen. We carry out a systematical study of the size scaling of Liouvillian gap in boundary-dissipated one-dimensional quasiperiodic and disorder systems. By treating the boundary-dissipation operators as a perturbation, we derive an analytical expression of the Liouvillian gap, which indicates clearly the Liouvillian gap being proportional to the minimum of boundary densities of eigenstates of the underlying Hamiltonian, and thus give a theoretical explanation why the Liouvillian gap has different size scaling relation in the extended and localized phase.

arxiv-2303-13066.title: Action principle of Galilean relativistic Proca theory
arxiv-2303-13066.creator: Rabin Banerjee, Soumya Bhattacharya
arxiv-2303-13066.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Rabin Banerjee, Soumya Bhattacharya. In this paper, we discuss Galilean relativistic Proca theory in detail. We first provide a set of mapping relations, derived systematically, that connect the covariant and contravariant vectors in the Lorentz relativistic and Galilean relativistic formulations. Exploiting this map, we construct the two limits of Galilean relativistic Proca theory from usual Proca theory in the potential formalism for both contravariant and covariant vectors which are now distinct entities.

arxiv-2311-08081.title: Evolutionary-enhanced quantum supervised learning model
arxiv-2311-08081.creator: Anton Simen, Rodrigo Bloot, Otto M. Pires, Erick G. Sperandio Nascimento
arxiv-2311-08081.description: Abstract Quantum supervised learning, utilizing variational circuits, stands out as a promising technology for NISQ devices due to its efficiency in hardware resource utilization during the creation of quantum feature maps and the implementation of hardware-efficient ansatz with trainable parameters.

arxiv-2411-12733.title: On the microscopics of proximity effects in one-dimensional superconducting hybrid systems
arxiv-2411-12733.creator: Siddhant Midha, Roshni Singh, Kaveh Gharavi, Jonathan Baugh, Bhaskaran Muralidharan
arxiv-2411-12733.description: Abstract Investigating the microscopic details of the proximity effect is crucial for both key experimental applications and fundamental inquiries into nanoscale devices featuring superconducting elements. In this work, we develop a framework motivated by experiments to study induced superconducting correlations in hybrid nanoscale devices featuring layered superconductor-normal heterostructures using the Keldysh non-equilibrium Green’s functions.

arxiv-2505-20662.title: AutoReproduce : Automatic AI Experiment Reproduction with Paper Lineage
arxiv-2505-20662.creator: Xuanle Zhao, Zilin Sang, Yuxuan Li, Qi Shi, Weilun Zhao, Shuo Wang, Duzhen Zhang, Xu Han, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun
arxiv-2505-20662.description: Abstract Efficient reproduction of research papers is pivotal to accelerating scientific progress. However, the increasing complexity of proposed methods often renders reproduction a labor-intensive endeavor, necessitating profound domain expertise. To address this, we introduce the paper lineage, which systematically mines implicit knowledge from the cited literature.

arxiv-2508-10596.title: A Unified Framework from Boltzmann Transport to Proton Treatment Planning Thanks: Department of Statistics, University of Warwick, Coventry CV4 7AL, UK. andreas.kyprianou@warwick.ac.uk . Thanks: Department of Mathematical Sciences, University of Bath, Bath BA2 7AY, UK. arp46@bath.ac.uk, tmp38@bath.a
arxiv-2508-10596.creator: Andreas E. Kyprianou, Aaron Pim, Tristan Pryer
arxiv-2508-10596.description: Abstract . This work develops a rigorous mathematical formulation of proton transport by integrating both deterministic and stochastic perspectives. The deterministic framework is based on the Boltzmann-Fokker-Planck equation, formulated as an operator equation in a suitable functional setting. The stochastic approach models proton evolution via a track-length parameterised diffusion process, whose infinitesimal generator provides an alternative description of transport.

arxiv-2511-04061.title: Fast Transport of Trapped Ultracold Atoms Using Shortcuts-to-Adiabaticity by Counterdiabatic Driving
arxiv-2511-04061.creator: Denuwan Vithanage, Skyler Wright, Edith Luveina-Joseph
arxiv-2511-04061.description: Abstract We numerically study the fast spatial transport of a trapped Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) using shortcuts-to-adiabaticity (STA) by counterdiabatic driving (CD). The trapping potential and the required auxiliary potential were simulated as painted potentials. We compared STA transport to transport that follows a constant-acceleration scheme (CA).

arxiv-2512-05959.title: M4-RAG : A Massive-Scale Multilingual Multi-Cultural Multimodal RAG
arxiv-2512-05959.creator: David Anugraha, Patrick Amadeus Irawan, Anshul Singh, En-Shiun Annie Lee, Genta Indra Winata
arxiv-2512-05959.description: Abstract Vision–language models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance in visual question answering (VQA), yet they remain constrained by static training data. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) mitigates this limitation by enabling access to up-to-date, culturally grounded, and multilingual information; however, multilingual multimodal RAG remains largely underexplored.

pmc-10538026.title: Growing in Saltwater: Biotechnological Potential of Novel Methylotuvimicrobium- and Methylomarinum-like Methanotrophic Bacteria
pmc-10538026.creator: Ekaterina N. Tikhonova, Ruslan Z. Suleimanov, Igor Y. Oshkin, Aleksey A. Konopkin, Diana V. Fedoruk, Nikolai V. Pimenov, Svetlana N. Dedysh
pmc-10538026.description: Methanotrophic bacteria that possess a unique ability of using methane as a sole source of carbon and energy have attracted considerable attention as potential producers of a single-cell protein. So far, this biotechnology implied using freshwater methanotrophs, although many regions of the world have limited freshwater resources.

pmc-10662033.title: Preparation of boron nitride nanosheets by glucose-assisted ultrasonic cavitation exfoliation
pmc-10662033.creator: Lian Zhou, Bo Zhang, Fuzhu Li, Ying Yan, Yun Wang, Ruitao Li
pmc-10662033.description: Boron nitride nanosheets (BNNSs) have been widely used in many fields due to their excellent properties. However, low preparation rates and difficulty in functionalization hinder their further development. This study proposes a novel glucose-assisted ultrasonic cavitation exfoliation (GAUCE) method with glucose as an auxiliary solution to prepare BNNSs. Results show that the method has a high preparation yield of 55.

pmc-10672164.title: Systems Biology in Cancer Diagnosis Integrating Omics Technologies and Artificial Intelligence to Support Physician Decision Making
pmc-10672164.creator: Alaa Fawaz, Alessandra Ferraresi, Ciro Isidoro
pmc-10672164.description: Cancer is the second major cause of disease-related death worldwide, and its accurate early diagnosis and therapeutic intervention are fundamental for saving the patient’s life. Cancer, as a complex and heterogeneous disorder, results from the disruption and alteration of a wide variety of biological entities, including genes, proteins, mRNAs, miRNAs, and metabolites, that eventually emerge as clinical symptoms.

pmc-11540583.title: Retrospective analysis of arginase 1 deficiency progression in adults over 5 years at a single metabolic centre
pmc-11540583.creator: Reena Sharma, John Bassett, Karolina M Stepien, Andrew Oldham, Ana Jovanovic, Alison Woodall, Diane Green
pmc-11540583.description: BackgroundThe clinical presentation of ARG1‐D is characterised by elevated arginine levels leading to neurological and mobility impairments. Information about long‐term outcomes in adults is lacking, which prompted us to undertake a retrospective observational study.MethodsWe extracted ARG1‐D patient data spanning a 5‐year period from electronic health records. Ethical approval was not required for the study. Informed consent was obtained.

pmc-11692206.title: FAMILY EXPERIENCE IN USING TELEPRESENCE ROBOTS WITH RESIDENTS IN LONG-TERM CARE
pmc-11692206.creator: Lillian Hung, Grace Hu, Joey Wong, Haopu (Lily) Ren, Jim Mann, Lily Wong
pmc-11692206.description: Informal care, most often provided by family or friends, remains a hidden and underrecognized undertaking within long-term care (LTC) settings. As care recipients transition into LTC, informal care partners experience a parallel shift in their caregiving roles: transitioning from primary care partner to visitor.

pmc-12589392.title: Machine learning models predict mortality risk in diabetic neuropathy patients using MIMIC-IV data
pmc-12589392.creator: Yanyi Huang, Wei Mo, Yang Liu, Shuanglin Wang, Yanping Zeng, Pingping Jiang, He Wang, Jianlu Bi
pmc-12589392.description: We aimed to construct and validate interpretable models for predicting mortality risk using machine learning (ML) methods to identify the risk factors associated with mortality in patients with diabetic neuropathy (DN). We selected patients from the US-based critical care database (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-IV)).

pmc-12732932.title: Reliability, Validity, and Optimal Cut-Off Scores of Action Research Arm Test and Jebsen–Taylor Hand Function Test in People with Parkinson’s Disease
pmc-12732932.creator: Sefa Eldemir, Burhanettin Cigdem, Daniele Giansanti
pmc-12732932.description: Highlights What are the main findings? The Jebsen–Taylor Hand Function Test demonstrated excellent test–retest reliability, concurrent validity, and discriminant validity, with derived cut-off scores (ranging from 3.56 to 64.23) that effectively discriminated between patients with Parkinson’s disease and healthy controls.

pmc-12818744.title: Understanding Biases in Liquid–Liquid Phase Separation: Investigating Amino Acid Enrichments in Phase-Separating Proteins toward Peptide Design
pmc-12818744.creator: Joana Calvário, Diogo Antunes, Rita Cipriano, Daniela Kalafatovic, Goran Mauša, Ana S. Pina
pmc-12818744.description: Liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) facilitates the formation of membraneless organelles, enhancing biochemical processes. The stickers-and-spacers model explains LLPS but is mainly validated in prion-like RNA-binding proteins. To broaden our understanding, we investigated peptide motifs associated with LLPS across diverse protein contexts using a computational approach on the droplet-promoting regions (DPRs) of 178 phase-separating proteins.

pmc-13038637.title: Effect of droplet size on the encapsulation efficiency of microparticles in passive microfluidic systems
pmc-13038637.creator: Risa Fujita, Masashi Kobayashi, Takashi Tanii, Masahiro Furuya, Shuichi Shoji, Daiki Tanaka
pmc-13038637.description: Droplet microfluidic technologies are widely used in single-cell analysis, in which passive encapsulation methods are commonly used to isolate individual cells or particles. In these systems, the number of particles per droplet is assumed to follow a Poisson distribution. However, the extent to which droplet size affects encapsulation behavior under passive conditions is poorly understood.

pmc-13295182.title: O-arm navigation vs. freehand screw placement in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: A comparative analysis of screw size and reoperation rates
pmc-13295182.creator: Rahul Ramanathan, Connor Luck, Özgür Dede, Timothy Ward
pmc-13295182.description: Objective:Pedicle screw fixation is the gold standard for surgical correction of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS). Prior to the adoption of intraoperative O-arm navigation, surgeons relied on freehand pedicle screw insertion. While freehand insertion demonstrates acceptable safety, comparative data on screw size selection between techniques remain limited.

pmc-13307072.title: Designing Thermomechanically Stable Nanocrystalline Alloys for Low Friction and Wear: A Perspective
pmc-13307072.creator: Frank W. DelRio, Rachel A. Knapp, Nicolas Argibay, Michael Chandross, Tomas F. Babuska, John F. Curry
pmc-13307072.description: In this Perspective, we discuss recent work and future trends on the usage of thermomechanically stable and self-lubricating nanocrystalline (NC) alloys for low friction and wear applications. The theoretical underpinnings and mechanistic framework for attaining and maintaining low friction and wear in metal contacts are presented.

pmc-13357976.title: Proliferation of pleural mesothelioma cells is enhanced by the microRNA-197-3p activity
pmc-13357976.creator: Ilaria Bononi, Giulia Di Mauro, Maria Letizia Tramarin, Valentina Esposito, Giulia Tonnini, Lucia Oton-Gonzalez, Beatrice Dallan, Elena Torreggiani, Fernanda Martini, Mauro Tognon
pmc-13357976.description: Human Pleural Mesothelioma (HPM) is an aggressive asbestos-related tumor with limited treatment options and a poor prognosis. MicroRNAs (miRNAs), known to play key roles in the pathogenesis of HPM, have emerged as promising candidates for both diagnostic and therapeutic applications. Among them, miR-197-3p has been previously identified as dysregulated in sera from HPM patients and workers ex-exposed to asbestos fibers.

pmc-13605891.title: Effect of Time–Temperature Modulation Combined with Residual Heating on Flavor and Texture Attributes of Steamed Perch Fish
pmc-13605891.creator: Yaling Yang, Lijin Wang, Feng Zhu, Huanlu Song, Yanbo Wang
pmc-13605891.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). To optimize the steaming process parameters for perch fish and improve its flavor quality, this study systematically compared dual-stage steaming (low–high temperature and high–low temperature) and residual-heat steaming (dual-stage steaming followed by heat retention) with traditional single-stage steaming. Dual-stage steaming (especially 80 °C → 100 °C) produced significant treatment effects in texture and umami-related measures, while several volatile aroma compounds showed significant treatment effects (p < 0.05) and had higher measured concentrations under residual-heat steaming.

uslaw-usc-t41-s8705.title: 41 U.S.C. § 8705 — Administrative offsets
uslaw-usc-t41-s8705.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t41-s8705.description: United States Code, Title 41 (Public Contracts); Chapter 87 (Kickbacks). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Definition.— In this section, the term “contracting officer” has the meaning given that term in chapter 71 of this title. (b) Offset Authority.— A contracting officer of a contracting agency may offset the amount of a kickback provided, accepted, or charged in violation of section 8702.

uslaw-usc-t42-s5196d.title: 42 U.S.C. § 5196d — Use of funds to prepare for and respond to hazards
uslaw-usc-t42-s5196d.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s5196d.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 68 (Disaster Relief); Subchapter IV–B (Emergency Preparedness); Part A (Powers And Duties). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Funds made available to the States under this subchapter may be used by the States for the purposes of preparing for hazards and providing emergency assistance in response to hazards. Regulations prescribed to carry.
